subject.title: refactor: consolidate Knip into a single config

question: Should OpenClaw adopt one convention-driven Knip configuration and accept the coupled upgrade to Knip 6.29.0 as the repository-wide dead-code-gate model?
rationale: The PR deliberately replaces established audit boundaries and detection semantics, and its author explicitly requested maintainer appetite before investing further; correctness checks alone cannot choose the preferred long-term tooling contract.

options.title: Sponsor the consolidation
options.body: Confirm the one-config/two-mode model, then require a rebase and comparative audit evidence before normal merge review.

options.title: Keep specialized audits
options.body: Retain the existing three-config split and close this refactor if explicit audit ownership is preferred over convention-based discovery.

options.title: Narrow the change
options.body: Accept a separately reviewed Knip upgrade or a targeted duplication reduction, but keep distinct audit configurations until equivalent coverage is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the consolidation
recommendation.body: Confirm the one-config/two-mode model, then require a rebase and comparative audit evidence before normal merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-wide CI policy and maintenance direction are the unresolved decision, rather than a narrow code repair.
